title: PromoSlot: outbound content calendar
description:
Parked design spec only — do not implement from this issue until explicitly prioritized.

## Why

Babulus is marketing automation. Inbound already exists (WaitlistSignup, MarketingLead, MarketingProgram, enrollments, MarketingInteraction for email/SMS). There is no outbound calendar. Publicist needs one.

Constraints:
- Do not smash this into MarketingInteraction (that is a touch to a lead).
- Do not add a Papyrus newsroom promote stage.
- Do not stand up a spreadsheet as source of truth.

## Object: PromoSlot

One row = one thing we might say, on one channel, on one day. A published article can spawn several slots over two weeks.

Fields:
- **when**: date and time, America/New_York
- **track**: `anthus` | `b0rd`
- **channel**: `linkedin` | `discord` | `x` | `etsy` (do not add Facebook in v1)
- **status**: `draft` → `ready` → `approved` → `queued` → `posted` | `skipped`
- **blurb**: the actual words
- **link**: canonical URL
- **source**: optional article slug or newsroom id
- **asset**: optional image or Babulus video id
- **live_url**: filled only after it went out
- **approved_by** / **approved_at**: Ryan, required before queued

## Status rules

Publicist drafts. Ryan must approve before queued. Babulus only moves approved → queued once a connector exists. Until then, approved is the finish line and a human pastes. Nothing posts live unless Ryan says so.

## How a published piece enters

Newsroom story still ends at published. Publicist then cuts three slots, not a new essay:

1. **LinkedIn**, day-of or next weekday morning — excerpt + link
2. **Discord**, same day — shorter pointer
3. **LinkedIn**, 4–7 days later — second angle or an older related piece

B0rd is the same object, different track. Quiet until there is a shop link or a Workbench post worth showing.

## Out of scope for this issue

- Do not implement the model yet.
- Do not wire SES, LinkedIn, Discord, or X.
- Do not build an admin UI.

This issue is the parked spec only.

title: Wire Python marketing runtime to new signups (event-driven: DynamoDB stream → Lambda → evaluate_rules/outbound_email)
description: Wire the Python marketing runtime (services/marketing-runtime) to new signups so that actions (e.g. welcome email, rule evaluation) run automatically.
